svg.title: Topology and edge loops: how a click becomes a loop
svg.desc: The mesh is a plain list of points and triangles. A topology is worked out from it: points on one spot become a vertex, flat neighbouring triangles join into quads, the sides of the faces are the edges. A click picks the nearest edge on the screen; the loop walks straight on at four-quad vertices, the ring walks across quads. The result is a list of points that all the tools already understand.
svg.text: Topology and edge loops (Phase 13, steps 3 and 4)
The mesh stays a plain list. The structure is worked out when needed, so every tool keeps working on points.
Stored mesh
points (x, y, z)
triangles (3 point numbers)
a cube has 24 points, 12
triangles; never changes shape
buildTopology
Derived topology (never saved)
1. Vertex = all points on one spot (3 per cube corner become 1)
2. Face = a quad when two flat triangles share their LONGEST side (the diagonal), else a triangle
3. Edge = a side of a face (a quad's diagonal is not an edge)
cube: 8 vertices, 6 quads, 12 edges · each edge knows its faces, each vertex its edges
Loop and ring on a grid of quads
loop
ring
Loop: straight on at each 4-quad vertex.
Ring: from edge to the edge across the quad. A loop cut goes across a ring.
What a click does
Points (1): nearest point, welded points together
Edges (2): nearest edge within 12 px
Alt + click = its loop · Loop / Ring buttons grow it
Faces (3): the face under the pointer (a quad is one)
Alt + click = the whole flat area
The result is a list of POINTS
an edge = its two ends, a face = its corners, a loop = every point on it
So move, turn, scale, delete and extrude work unchanged.
Edges with both ends selected are drawn in the selection colour.
Loops stop at triangles, poles (not 4 edges) and seams.
